correctness.rationale: For every m,n>=2 spectral clipping is the Frobenius projector. At Z_s=(1+s)uv^T its derivative tends the tangent hyperplane map J_G=I-G tensor G. Its induced max-entry row norm has the explicit formula in the proof; Cauchy and equal-tail attainment optimize over unit singular vectors. At any almost-everywhere Euclidean projector derivative the symmetric positive contraction 0<=J<=I bounds an absolute row sum by (1+sqrt(mn))/2; mollification and segment integration give the full two-input bound. The 2-by-2 equality, square dimension growth and rank-one tangential asymptotic follow algebraically. Supplementary finite checks pass but do not replace proof.

value.rationale: Spectral-norm-ball projection is standard in conic and regularized matrix processing. Exact robust entrywise error budgets are not implied by Frobenius nonexpansivity. The theorem gives a dimension-linear instability mechanism, a sharp family of boundary tangents, a two-variable maximization valid in every rectangular dimension, and an exact 2-by-2 global coefficient; it explicitly leaves the general global sharp coefficient open. These are structural sensitivity facts about an intrinsic operation, not a parameter rename or arbitrary finite sample.
